adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:57 — Status is saved to ERROR outside any transaction before the incident get_or_create, so a crash or DB error mid-way leaves the env stuck in ERROR with no active incident, and every later failure takes the ERROR branch with incident None, producing no occurrences (pre-existing, moved verbatim).

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` (src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py), when `monitor_env.status` is OK/ACTIVE the code sets `monitor_env.status = MonitorStatus.ERROR` and immediately `monitor_env.save(update_fields=("status",))` before calling `MonitorIncident.objects.get_or_create(...)`. There is no surrounding transaction/atomic block in the diff. If the process crashes or `get_or_create` raises after the status save, the environment can remain in ERROR without an active incident. Later failures will take the `elif monitor_env.status == MonitorStatus.ERROR` branch where `incident = monitor_env.active_incident` may be `None`, and occurrence creation is skipped due to `... and incident` guard, matching the finding's scenario. (This appears moved from the old code, but it is still a real correctness defect present in the diff.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:62 — The read-then-write on monitor_env.status plus get_or_create(monitor_environment, resolving_checkin=None) is not locked, so concurrent failing check-ins for one env can both see OK and create duplicate open incidents (or hit MultipleObjectsReturned) unless a DB unique constraint exists (pre-existing, moved).

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` (new `incidents.py`), the code branches on `monitor_env.status` and then performs `monitor_env.status = MonitorStatus.ERROR; monitor_env.save(...)` followed by `MonitorIncident.objects.get_or_create(monitor_environment=monitor_env, resolving_checkin=None, ...)` without any explicit transaction/row lock (`select_for_update`) around the read/modify/write. As shown in the diff, nothing prevents two concurrent failing check-ins from both observing `OK/ACTIVE` and racing through the update + `get_or_create`, which can result in multiple open incidents unless a DB-level uniqueness constraint exists for `(monitor_environment, resolving_checkin)` (not verifiable from this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:84 — In the ERROR branch, monitor_env.active_incident can be None (e.g. after a partial failure or manual status change); the occurrence is then silently skipped but the function still returns True and fires monitor_environment_failed, so nothing surfaces the missing incident (pre-existing).

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` (new `src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py`), the `MonitorStatus.ERROR` branch sets `incident = monitor_env.active_incident` without guaranteeing it exists. If it is `None`, the later guard `... and incident:` skips `create_incident_occurrence`, but the function still unconditionally calls `monitor_environment_failed.send(...)` and returns `True`. This yields a “success”/failure-signal path with no incident/occurrence created, which is a concrete inconsistent behavior present in the post-diff code (even if it may have been pre-existing before the refactor).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:94 — When the threshold is crossed, one Kafka occurrence is produced per check-in, all with the same fingerprint and the same aggregate failure reason, from an unordered queryset; a failure mid-loop leaves partial occurrences with no retry because status is already ERROR (pre-existing).

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` the code does `checkins = MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(id__in=[...])` and then loops `for checkin in checkins: create_incident_occurrence(previous_checkins, checkin, ...)`, which will emit one occurrence per returned check-in while `get_failure_reason(failed_checkins)` is computed from the same `previous_checkins` list each time (so the “aggregate” reason is duplicated across occurrences) and the queryset ordering is unspecified. The additional claim about partial production/no retry if Kafka production fails mid-loop is a plausible robustness concern given `monitor_env.status` is saved to ERROR before producing and there’s no transaction/exception handling shown, but the failure behavior is not directly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:48 — With threshold > 1, fewer than threshold prior check-ins (e.g. a brand-new monitor with a single failure) still passes the no-OK check and opens an incident early, because the list length is never compared with failure_issue_threshold (pre-existing).

adjudication.rationale: In src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py, when failure_issue_threshold > 1 the code slices `previous_checkins[:failure_issue_threshold]` and reverses it, but never verifies `len(previous_checkins) == failure_issue_threshold` before proceeding. If there are fewer than `failure_issue_threshold` check-ins (e.g. a new monitor with only 1 failed check-in), the `any(checkin["status"] == OK ...)` guard will be false and the code will still set `monitor_env.status = ERROR` and create/get an incident, effectively triggering an incident early.
